name: air-route
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. A finished SQUARE 1:1 anatomy teaching illustration for Body School, ages 11–13. White background, navy bold sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, gentle shaded textbook anatomy matching the bones lesson. Exact title "Air travels into your lungs". Main image: side-facing head profile with nose and mouth air passage continuing into trachea, connected to front-facing two pink lungs with a branching bronze airway tree. Simplified torso outline, no heart or blood vessels. Clear navy arrows trace inhaled air nose/mouth -> windpipe -> branching airways into BOTH lungs. Readable labels with accurate leader lines: "Nose and mouth", "Windpipe", "Branching airways". Small circular magnification inset lower corner shows grape-like cluster of tiny pale pink air sacs at the end of a small airway, label "Air sacs". Leader from inset to peripheral lung region. Keep airway anatomy plausible, trachea must split into TWO main branches, avoid throat-to-esophagus confusion. Do not put arrows into lung tissue beyond airway terminals. Enough margins; no watermark; no extra small text.

name: gas-exchange
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished SQUARE 1:1 textbook diagram for Body School ages 11–13. White background, bold navy sans-serif lettering, pale blue label panels, soft shaded pink tissues and red blood cells. Exact title "Air sacs exchange gases". Large simplified CUTAWAY of ONE air sac on the LEFT, its hollow air-filled interior visible; an airway neck enters upper left. On the RIGHT a capillary curves closely alongside the thin sac wall but remains a SEPARATE enclosed channel containing red blood cells. Clear adjacent thin air-sac and capillary walls, no opening between air and blood. A large orange arrow labeled "Oxygen" goes FROM air-sac interior across walls INTO blood on right. A large teal arrow labeled "Carbon dioxide" at a different height goes FROM blood on right across walls INTO air-sac interior on left. Arrowheads must point in opposite correct directions. Labels "Air sac", "Capillary", "Thin walls", "Red blood cell" with accurate leaders. Bottom short captions "Oxygen: air sac to blood" and "Carbon dioxide: blood to air sac". Airway connects only to air sac, not vessel. No blue blood, no excessive molecule symbols, no watermark. Spacious readable diagram.

name: heart-and-vessels
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished WIDE landscape 2:1 anatomy illustration for Body School ages 11–13. White background, bold navy headings, pale blue label panels, softly shaded red tissues and ivory highlights, elegant clean textbook illustration. Exact title "The heart pumps; vessels carry". Main diagram spans left two-thirds: small simplified red anatomical heart at LEFT, a thick-walled artery carries blood RIGHTWARD along TOP toward a fine capillary network at RIGHT beside body cells, and a thin-walled vein carries blood LEFTWARD along BOTTOM back to heart. Use bright red for artery and dark burgundy for vein, NOT blue blood. Large clear arrowheads show artery away from heart and vein toward heart. Labels "Heart", "Artery: away from heart", "Vein: toward heart", "Capillaries". Small cross-section cut ends visually show thicker artery wall and thinner vein wall with a valve inside vein. The RIGHT THIRD is a clearly bordered enlarged inset titled "At the body cells": one capillary segment containing red blood cells beside body cells. One orange arrow FROM blood to cells labeled "Oxygen and nutrients"; one teal arrow FROM cells into blood labeled "Waste". All vessels continuous in main diagram, no lungs or second circuit, no chamber anatomy. Legible large lettering; no tiny text or watermark.

name: blood-journey
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished PORTRAIT 4:5 diagram for Body School ages 11–13. White background, bold navy sans-serif lettering, pale blue label panels, gentle shaded textbook organs. Exact title "Follow the blood's journey". Lungs centered TOP, simplified heart icon centered MIDDLE, cluster of body cells centered BOTTOM. Show TWO linked circulation loops, with two separate flow lanes through the heart, no named chambers and no mixing lane. UPPER loop: dark burgundy arrow from heart UP the LEFT to lungs, then bright red arrow from lungs DOWN the RIGHT to heart. LOWER loop: bright red arrow from heart DOWN the RIGHT to body cells, then dark burgundy arrow from body cells UP the LEFT to heart. Each path large, clear, with unambiguous arrowheads. The four directed connections must be exactly heart->lungs, lungs->heart, heart->body, body->heart. Labels "Lungs", "Heart", "Body cells". By lungs, two short notes "Oxygen enters blood" and "Carbon dioxide leaves blood". By body cells, notes "Oxygen leaves blood" and "Carbon dioxide enters blood". Bottom legend has bright red swatch "More oxygen" and dark burgundy swatch "Less oxygen", then "Blood is always red." No blue blood. Do not draw shortcut from lungs to body or bypass heart. Clean spacious schematic, no decorative arteries, no watermark.
